_about: P25.2.4 analogy visuals: the writer may attach ONE analogy to a segment (at most max_per_episode), picked only from these treatments and images, so the same choice always renders the same way. Where to use what: `when` is what the writer reads. Images are sourced once by visual-sourcing (judged) and reused from research/assets/visuals. Rule (Talha, 29 Oct): every picture is offered and searched at make time; an approved one is reused from the library for good, a miss is searched again next episode; a picture used in the last reuse_after episodes is not offered.

compare.when: a number or thing is hard to feel, and one everyday object makes it click (a chip the size of a rice grain; revenue = a year of chai sales)
compare.fields: left: image id, right: image id, left_label, right_label (max 18 chars each), joiner: '=' or 'vs' or '≈'

scale.when: a multiplier or big count (100x cheaper, 60,000 workers): one everyday image repeated in a grid with the multiplier
scale.fields: image: image id, big: the multiplier or count as shown in the facts (e.g. '100x'), label (max 24 chars)

photo.when: the witty line names an everyday scene the viewer pictures at once (Mumbai local at 9 am, a traffic jam, a wedding baraat)
photo.fields: image: image id, caption (max 30 chars, the punchline)

stamp.when: a deadpan verdict on the story (OUCH, PLOT TWIST, BIG IF TRUE, NOT YET): a rubber stamp slams over the graphic
